decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0% to 0.25%. The vote was 10-2. Dissenting: James Bullard, Esther L. George.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in May suggests that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in March suggests that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace.”

changes.quote: Labor market conditions have shown further improvement in recent months, on balance, but the unemployment rate remains elevated.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Labor market conditions have shown some improvement in recent months, on balance, but the unemployment rate remains elevated.”

changes.quote: Partly reflecting transitory influences, inflation has been running below the Committee's longer-run objective, but longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Inflation has been running somewhat below the Committee's longer-run objective, apart from temporary variations that largely reflect fluctuations in energy pric…”

changes.quote: Longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: The Committee sees the downside risks to the outlook for the economy and the labor market as having diminished since the fall.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Committee continues to see downside risks to the economic outlook.”

tone_quotes.quote: In particular, the Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and currently anticipates that this exceptionally low range for the federal funds rate will be appropriate at least as long as the unemployment rate remains above 6-1/2 percent, inflation between one and two years ahead is projected to be no more than a half percentage point above the Committee's 2 percent longer-run goal, and longer-term inflation expectations continue to be well anchored.
The Committee sees the downside risks to the outlook for the economy and the labor market as having diminished since the fall.
Taken together, these actions should maintain downward pressure on longer-term interest rates, support mortgage markets, and help to make broader financial conditions more accommodative.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 11.94% APR costs about $49.75 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.33% and moved +13 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.91% would rise by about $22.45 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 7.5%, and employers added an average of 183k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.4% over the past year (May 2013); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.4%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +4 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.07% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 80%, cut 19%, hike 1%.
